title: Customer region gating and prioritization framework
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: Provide a deterministic, low-friction path to intake, evaluate, and prioritize customer requests for new region availability and data-residency constraints (including failover, geo-fencing, and contractual residency terms).

Scope: non-bug customer requests that require product & infra changes (new region provisioning, residency guarantees, failover geography, or contractual residency clauses). Excludes: one-off enterprise contractual negotiations that require legal-only solutions, and routine capacity scaling for existing regions.

Core deliverables in this ticket:
- An intake form template (fields + validation) for Sales/CS/SEs to submit region/residency requests.
- A prioritization scorecard with weighted criteria and thresholds that map to three outcome lanes: Expedite, Standard, Defer.
- A minimal artifact checklist required for a request to be considered (security/compliance artifacts, data flow diagrams, customer SLAs).
- Lead time and cost estimate templates by region class (edge, secondary, primary) with staffing and infra cost heuristics.
- Approval matrix (who signs off for expedite vs standard) and a runbook for failover testing and rollback.
- Tabulated examples that illustrate scoring using three recent anonymized customer asks.

Intake form (high level fields):
- Customer name & account ID
- Request type: New region | Residency guarantee | Failover target | Cross-border data flow exception
- Primary region requested and secondary failover region(s)
- Regulatory/contractual requirement citation (e.g., GDPR, CCPA, sector-specific)
- Data classification (PII, PHI, low-sensitivity)
- Estimated QPS and concurrency at go-live and steady-state
- Required SLOs (p99 latency, availability) and escalation SLA
- Commercial commitment (MRC/ARR or strategic priority)
- Desired timeline and business justification
- Attachments: contract excerpt, DF diagram, security controls checklist

Prioritization scorecard (weights recommended):
- Business impact (ARR or strategic: 30%)
- Compliance & legal risk (mandatory/regulatory: 25%)
- Technical feasibility & infra runway (engineering effort + ops risk: 20%)
- Cost to operate (ongoing infra + bandwidth: 15%)
- Customer urgency & PR multiplier (pilot/strategic: 10%)
Thresholds: total >= 75 -> Expedite (fast-track, dedicated SCRUM lane); 50-74 -> Standard (regular planning); <50 -> Defer (review quarterly).

Minimal artifact checklist (must be present for triage):
- Signed T&C/contract snippet requiring residency or region availability
- Data flow diagram showing systems touching the data
- Security controls map (KMS/HSM, VPC, logging/audit requirements)
- Identified POC (Customer and Redwood owner) and target launch date

Operational assumptions & lead times (estimate):
- Edge/secondary region (pre-configured in cloud): 4-6 weeks
- Primary region with new residency guarantees (legal & infra): 8-12 weeks
- On-prem/VPC private deployment (customer-managed infra): 12+ weeks
- Failover-only requests (no residency): 2-4 weeks for routing + validation
Notes: lead times assume no dedicated hardware procurement; quantized estimates will be attached per region when the infra team provides capacity templates.

Failover & compatibility policy summary:
- Default policy: geo-failover to nearest compatible region with same model family and quantization profile.
- If customer requires read-only residency, we recommend prefix caching + synchronous write replication only to residency region and async to others (documented risks).
- For policies that request hard residency (data cannot leave region), require end-to-end audit proof and legal sign-off; these requests are auto-elevated to Expedite if contractual.

Approval matrix:
- Expedite: Product Director + Infra Lead + Legal sign-off required
- Standard: Product Manager + Infrastructure SRE approval
- Defer: Product Manager or PMO review during quarterly prioritization

Artifacts & links (templates):
- Intake form template (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/region-intake-template
- Cost estimate spreadsheet (Drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/region-cost-template
- Failover playbook draft (GitHub gist): https://github.com/redwood-inference/failover-playbook-draft

Recommended next steps:
1) Validate intake form with Sales/CS/SEs in a 30-min sync (owner: Marcus Liu).
2) Pilot the scorecard with three recent requests (owner: Aisha Patel).
3) Iterate weights after pilot and publish triage rubric to Confluence.
4) Schedule an approvals working session with Legal & Infra.

Trade-offs & open questions:
- Weighting business impact higher risks prioritizing large customers over regulatory needs; propose hard floor for compliance score to prevent deprioritizing mandatory legal requests.
- Estimating cost vs time: offering faster lead times often requires more upfront infra commitment (reserved capacity) and higher unit costs. Need policy on cost pass-through to customers.

Success metrics:
- Time from intake to decision <= 5 business days for Standard lane, <= 48 hours for Expedite lane
- % of requests with complete artifact checklist on first submission >= 80% after training
- Lead time accuracy within +/-25% of actual for planned regions after 3 pilots

This ticket will produce the published intake template, the prioritization rubric, and a short how-to doc for Sales/CS. The operational runbook and cost templates will be owned by Infra and Finance respectively (see dependencies).
